question: Compare the magnetic field at equal distances on the axial line and equatorial line of a short bar magnet. Give reason for your answer.

options.A: At equal distances, the equatorial field is twice the axial field: $B_{\text{eq}}=2B_{\text{axial}}$.
options.B: At equal distances, axial and equatorial fields are equal because both vary as $1/r^3$.
options.C: The axial field is four times the equatorial field because the axial formula contains $2M$.
options.D: For a short bar magnet, $B_{\text{axial}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{2M}{r^3}$ and $B_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r^3}$. Thus, at the same distance, $B_{\text{axial}}:B_{\text{eq}}=2:1$.
